Suma was 29 year old, a newly pregnant woman, and her heart was full of joy.
But one day, she started feeling intense cramps and pain in her abdomen.
She thought , this is normal. It's just part of pregnancy and it will reduce as time passes.  So she ignored it. And ignored it. Until the bleeding started.
When she finally saw her doctor — she was told she had a miscarriage.

So what actually is miscarriage?
A miscarriage is the loss of pregnancy before the 20th week. The signs are always there — intense abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, lower back pain, pregnancy symptoms fading away.
If you are a mom-to-be and experiencing any of these — don't ignore it. Don't be like Suma.

Menopause is more than the end of periods — it’s a hormonal transition that can bring changes throughout the body. 
As estrogen and progesterone levels gradually decline, women may notice changes in sleep, energy, body temperature, mood, and overall wellbeing.
Understanding what is happening inside your body can help you recognise these changes and take better care of your health.
Because menopause is not just a phase to get through — it’s a phase to understand
